_comment: Advisories that `npm audit` reports but which are not reachable in this
application. Every entry must carry a justification and an expiry date.
This is NOT a way to defer work on an exploitable finding. An entry is only
legitimate when the vulnerable code path cannot be reached at all. If a fix
exists and is installable, bump the dependency instead.
Entries are checked by .github/scripts/audit-check.mjs. An expired entry is a
hard failure, so every suppression comes back for review on its own.
`workspaces` scopes an entry to the workspaces it was justified for, so a
suppression reasoned about one bot can never silently cover another package.

allow.title: Server-Side Request Forgery in Request
reason: matrix-bot-sdk 0.8.0, the latest release, depends on the deprecated
`request` through request-promise, and `request` has no patched version.
The advisory needs `request` to be pointed at a server an attacker controls,
which then redirects it across protocols. The SDK uses `request` only for the
Matrix homeserver the operator configured, and the bots' own outbound call,
to the n8n webhook, goes through axios to a URL from the environment. No URL
is ever taken from the content of a Matrix message.
Revisit when matrix-bot-sdk drops `request` or the SDK is replaced.

allow.title: uuid: missing buffer bounds check in v3/v5/v6 when buf is provided
reason: uuid 3.4.0 arrives through matrix-bot-sdk -> request-promise -> request,
which pins `uuid@^3.3.2`; the fix is in uuid 11.1.1 and cannot be installed
The advisory concerns v3(), v5() and v6() called with a caller-supplied
buffer. `request` is the only caller of uuid in the tree and calls it with no
arguments, the v4 path, which is not affected. Neither bot calls uuid itself.
Revisit together with the `request` entry above.
